newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- LONDON IS LEADING CENTRE FOR CREDIT DERIVATIVES

New York has been overtaken by London as the leading centre for the market in credit derivatives. Credit derivatives allow banks to insure against the risks that their borrowers will not repay them. The London market has contracts covering $20 billion (12.1bn stg) of loans which, according to a survey by British Bankers Association (BBA), now outstrips the New York market. The BBA survey also claims that the London market has half of the world market in credit derivatives.
-- ARMED TAX POLICE RAID SAATCHI MOSCOW OPERATION

The Moscow office of British-based advertising agency Saatchi and Saatchi has been raided by armed tax police. The raid is part of a crackdown on foreign companies in Russia. The authorities have accused Saatchi and Saatchi of owing Rbs33bn (3.3 million stg) in taxes and fines. According to the Russian police the tax debt relates to a German-based company, Zoom Media, which they allege had been trading on behalf of Saatchi and Saatchi.
-- CUSTOMS & EXCISE JUDGED TO HAVE ACTED ILLEGALLY ON VAT

The High Court in London has ruled that the Customs & Excise acted illegally in anticipating the forthcoming Budget and refusing to repay companies VAT which they had overpaid for over a limit period of three years. The ruling could cost the government 35 million stg immediately and more over a period of time and is expected to increase pressure on the government to look once more at its plans to limit claims by companies for repayments to a three year period.
-- BBC IN DEMAND FOR EASIER ACCESS TO DIGITAL TV

The chairman of the BBC, Sir Christopher Bland, has issued a warning that there is a danger that News International could develop a virtual monopoly in the field of digital TV access in the UK. Speaking to the Westminster Media Forum, he complained that the issue of access to digital broadcasting was essential to UK programme makers if a situation in which News International was forced to divest itself of certain digital interests was to be avoided.
-- ROLE FOR COMPANIES IN SPENDING OF WINDFALL TAX REJECTED

Proposals from Labour deputy leader John Prescott that regional electricity and water companies be provided with a role in the training programmes to be funded by a windfall tax have been rejected by party leader Tony Blair. A spokesman for the leader noted that the companies would be obliged to pay any such levy and that what was done with the money subsequently was a matter for government. Labour is planning to raise in the region of 5bn stg in such a manner to be used in funding training programmes for the unemployed.
-- ALLIED COLLOIDS BUYS SUPPLIER FOR 390 MILLION DOLLARS

Speciality chemicals group Allied Colloids has acquired a US supplier, CPS, in a deal worth some $390 million. In order to fund the deal Allied Colloids plans a rights issue. Despite running counter to the general sector trend towards increasing business focus, the deal was generally welcomed by observers, who noted that it would provide potential for growth and costs savings.
-- VODAFONE BUYS PEOPLES PHONE FOR 77 MILLION STG

UK mobile phone operator Vodafone has acquired the distributed Peoples Phone in a deal worth 77 million stg. The deal will provide Vodafone with 400 retail outlets and help reduce the company's dependence on independents. Already Vodafone products accounted for some 90 per cent of the sales at Peoples Phone. News of the deal came as Vodafone announced a rise of 21 per cent in half-time interim pre-tax profits to 252 million stg.
-- CHAIRMAN OF GAN REFUSES DEMAND FOR RESIGNATION

The chairman of French state-owned insurance group GAN has refused a government demand for his resignation. Jean-Jacques Bonnaud had been asked to step down on the grounds that he had helped undermine the planned privatisation of GAN's 93 per cent owned banking subsidiary CIC. Bonnard has said that to resign would be "admitting to a fault which I do not feel I have committed". -- US UTILITY DENIES TALKS ON LONDON ELECTRICITY

US utility Entergy has denied newspaper reports that it is involved in talks with British regional electricity company London Electricity. Entergy said it is not involved in discussions with any English electricity company. However, the company refused to comment specifically on the reports linking it with a 1.2bn stg bid for London Electricity.
-- VIRGIN IN JOINT VENTURE TO OFFER INTERNET SERVICE

Leisure brand Virgin has launched Virgin Net, an internet joint venture with US-based International CableTel's Cable Online. The venture aims to attract 20,000 subscribers by the end of the year, and will be offered in outlets such as the Virgin Megastores. Virgin Net will also offer a home installation service to attract first-time users, and claims to be the first service provider to offer "intelligent agent" software for Internet searches.
